item.title: Tuckahoe boots Greenwich football from the Class D state playoffs on final play
item.description: Greenwich coach Brandon Linnett's team saw its season come to an end Friday with a state semifinal loss to Tuckahoe. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - Being in a tight state semifinal game at Middletown High School isn't a new experience for the Greenwich football team. Friday, the Witches found themselves in another tight tussle against Section 1 champion Tuckahoe. The game was tied late and the Tigers displayed a flair for the dramatic, first completing a 22-yard pass down to the Greenwich 10-yard line with four seconds remaining. From there, sophomore kicker Zander Gjeloshaj - who caught the pass to get the Tigers into field goal range - booted a 27-yard field goal as time expired as Tuckahoe registered a thrilling 17-14 victory over the Witches in the Class D state semifinals. "They made some nice plays down the stretch," Greenwich coach Brandon Linnett said. "They had a real good second half. We probably needed to be more than 6-0 at halftime. We dominated. Their defense dominated in the second half." Tuckahoe (8-3), ranked No. 2 in the state, did not score until the fourth quarter and still trailed 14-7 until 6-foot-5 junior tight end Luca DelConte caught a pass along the left sideline, stiff-armed a defender and proceeded to dash for a 64-yard touchdown. The Tigers added the extra-point boot to tie it with 3:55 left. On its ensuing possession, Greenwich reached the Tuckahoe 26-yard line and was stopped on downs with 1:23 left. The Tigers quickly drove down the field and converted a fourth-down pass to Gjeloshaj to set the stage for his game-winning field goal. "It just didn't go our way in the second half," said Greenwich junior Ethan Saunders, who shifted from wingback to quarterback following an injury suffered last week by sophomore quarterback Brett Traver. "It was a crazy game right down to the wire," Friday's result was the Witches' third consecutive painful conclusion at this stage of the state playoffs. Greenwich also fell to Tuckahoe 13-7 in last year's semifinals and dropped a 25-18 decision against Burke Catholic in the 2024 semifinals. "I am a little disappointed for my kids. Seniors, it is tough. It is always tough to say goodbye," Linnett said. "I understand what we have accomplished here. In a couple of days, they will, too." The Witches grabbed a 14-7 lead on a 3-yard Saunders touchdown run with 8:02 remaining. "Not having Brett was a big deal, but Ethan did a great job at quarterback. He made some big throws, and his legs were huge," Linnett said. "We adjusted what we had to do during the week and our kids adjusted well." Key moment The only reception of the game made by Gjeloshaj saw the sophomore catch the ball at around the 18 and work his way forward eight more yards. Justin Gjekaj, Tuckahoe's holder, snared a high snap and Gjeloshaj calmly pounded the ball through the uprights to end the game. item.title: Browns’ Delpit Couldn’t Help Himself From Trolling The Steelers
item.description: Grant Delpit has no chill. The Cleveland Browns defensive back talked to reporters on Friday, and before he finished his media session, he seemingly took a shot at the drama surrounding the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of Cleveland’s AFC North rivals. Delpit, who’s played his entire NFL career so far in Cleveland uniform, ended his talk with reporters with a “1, 2, 3 Browns” statement. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images On its own, that quote doesn’t seem anything remotely beyond normal. But given the wild drama that unfolded this week concerning Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers, it’s not hard to interpret Delpit’s words as a subtle (and hilarious) shot at Pittsburgh. When Rodgers decided to talk and appear on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday after Pittsburgh benched him, one of his head-turning comments was a story about Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy mistakenly saying “1, 2, 3 Packers” during a Pittsburgh huddle. Delpit is hardly the only one who’s made light of the fallout of Rodgers’ exit from the Steelers, but him being a Brown surely adds some flavor to his joke. Cleveland is coming off a Week 11 bye, so Delpit might also have some extra energy to keep up with the news around the league. item.description: San Diego State junior forward Bailey Barnhard (20) dribbles against Hawaii junior forward Zyriah Price on Friday, November 27, 2026 at the Rainbow Wahine Showdown at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center in Honolulu, Hawaii. Trailing by 7 points inside the final minute, the San Diego State Aztecs missed three consecutive 3-pointer attempts on a possession, which typified a frustrating afternoon in a 71-64 loss to the Hawaii Rainbow Wahine on Friday at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center. Junior forward Bailey Barnhard scored 17 points with 12 rebounds, her first career double-double, but SDSU (4-3) missed their first seven shots as Hawaii (2-5) opened with a 12-0 lead they never relinquished. Sophomore guard Bailey Flavell scored a career-high 28 points alongside 6 rebounds and 5 assists for the Rainbow Wahine, and junior center Ritoya Tamilo added 17 points and 6 rebounds. “(Hawaii) made some shots that we weren’t ready for. (Flavell) got hot and we couldn’t really do anything to slow her down, so giving up 28 points to a player, we knew we were going to have our hands full with (Tamilo’s) height…hats off to them, they beat us from the jump,” head coach Stacie Terry-Hutson said. In their second road game of the season, the Aztecs shot under 40% from the field in three of the four quarters, including a frigid fourth which saw the side make just 4-of-19 from the field. Senior guard Eva DeChent, who finished with 12 points before fouling out, and freshman forward Mayenabasi Akpan were the only players other than Barnhard to make a bucket in the final frame. Akpan played 6 of her 13 minutes in the fourth, putting up a tidy 7 points and 3 rebounds in her brief bits of action for the game. item.title: Steelers cap tumultuous week with 27-5 rout of Broncos
item.description: Pittsburgh's Jalen Ramsey returns an interception for a touchdown in the Steelers' NFL win over the Denver Broncos (Justin K. Aller) The Pittsburgh Steelers shook off the controversy sparked by star quarterback Aaron Rodgers's bitter midweek departure to dominate the Denver Broncos 27-5 in a key NFL clash on Friday. Mason Rudolph stepped in at quarterback and threw for 142 yards and one touchdown to wide receiver DK Metcalf, and the Steelers' defense scored two touchdowns as Pittsburgh ended the Broncos' six-game winning streak. Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt recovered a fumble by Broncos quarterback Bo Nix in the end zone for the Steelers' opening touchdown, and Jalen Ramsey ran a Nix interception back for a TD, Pittsburgh's defense harrying Nix into a series of uncharacteristic mistakes in difficult, rainy conditions. The Steelers remained unbeaten at home, improving to 7-4 as they at least temporarily put the ugly split from four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Rodgers aside. Rodgers, a Super Bowl champion who turns 43 next week, had been benched for the game amid a rift with Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy over the coach's offensive play calling. Rodgers then went on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show" and aired an array of complaints about the coach, alleging McCarthy had fallen asleep in team meetings and suggesting he wasn't fit for the job. Steelers owner Art Rooney II voiced support for McCarthy on Thursday, saying that "insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization." McCarthy and Steelers players had been tight-lipped in their responses in the days before the game, although Metcalf flashed eight fingers in a touchdown celebration interpreted as a reference to Rodgers's number eight. "At the end of the day, it's football, and we have a job to do as professionals to go out there and compete at the highest level and win games," said tight end Pat Freiermuth. "Regardless of the noise, it's our responsibility and our job to block out the noise." Rudolph said he appreciated the support he'd received from teammates after they were all rocked by the week's events. "They all had the same mixed emotions that I did, just shocked at what on earth just happened when you wake up on Wednesday morning," Rudolph said. "After the initial shocks sort of passed through, they just made it known that they were with me, behind me. It wasn't like a throw in the towel, season's over vibe." It was a damaging defeat for Denver, which fell to 8-3 to slip further behind the 10-1 Buffalo Bills in the race for the top seed in the AFC. They are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs atop the AFC West division. McCarthy called it a "special win" after back-to-back defeats that had helped ramp up the tensions within the team. "You look at what's happened the last two weeks, we needed a win. We needed a win, and it was old-fashioned. It was black and blue, downhill, just going after it, staying square, fundamental football." bb/des

item.title: Postgame Reaction: Avalanche Rally From Three-Goal Deficit to Beat Wild in Shootout
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What an incredible comeback. The Colorado Avalanche, without Nathan MacKinnon or Martin Necas , erased a three-goal deficit in the final 6:23 of regulation before beating the Minnesota Wild 4-3 in a shootout Friday at Grand Casino Arena. Trailing 3-0 late in the third period, Colorado mounted an improbable comeback to steal two points from the top team in the Central Division. Devon Toews , Artturi Lehkonen , and T.J. Hughes scored to even the game before the end of regulation. Hughes and Lehkonen also added assists. Mackenzie Blackwood made 19 saves, including a relatively quiet third period in which he faced just two shots. He didn’t see a single shot in overtime. Cale Makar provided the lone shootout goal among eight total attempts. It’s arguably the most impressive win of the season for the Avalanche, particularly given the circumstances. Following Wednesday’s victory over the Montreal Canadiens, Taylor Makar was called up to join the team on its road trip. Then, right before puck drop Friday, the Avalanche announced that Necas would miss the game with an upper-body injury . Hughes was promoted to the top line, while the younger Makar slotted into the third line. The Wild, meanwhile, were without Quinn Hughes and looking to rebound from their first regulation loss since Oct. 22. Their 12-0-3 stretch came to an end against the Utah Mammoth. Colorado dug itself an early hole in the first period, with two goals that were largely self-inflicted. First, Joel Eriksson Ek opened the scoring with an impressive individual effort after an Avalanche turnover at their own blue line. Blake Coleman then doubled the lead with a solo effort of his own, beating Blackwood on a shot the Colorado netminder would probably like to have back. The Avalanche didn’t have much going for them in the opening period, and that continued into the second. Their best opportunity came on a Hughes breakaway, but Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt came up with the stop. Eriksson Ek added his second of the night later in the period, sending Minnesota into the third with a comfortable 3-0 lead. Even with Colorado outshooting Minnesota early, it was difficult to envision the Avalanche having this kind of comeback in them. Head coach Jared Bednar pulled Blackwood with more than seven minutes remaining, shortly after Parker Kelly and Kirill Kaprizov were assessed matching minors. The resulting power play gave Colorado a 5-on-4 advantage, and Toews made it count. The defenseman scored his 10th goal of the season with just over six minutes remaining to get the comeback started. Colorado pulled Blackwood again, and Minnesota nearly put the game away with an empty-net goal. But Makar came up with a terrific defensive play to prevent it. The Avalanche quickly went the other way, and Makar’s point shot was redirected by Lehkonen to make it 3-2. The goal, Lehkonen’s 17th of the season, came with 3:59 remaining. item.description: Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall watches his players from the sidelines. The Florida Gators lead the Florida State Seminoles at the half 10-3 on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Florida delivered more than another rivalry victory Friday afternoon. The Gators also brought Florida State’s season to a painful conclusion. No. 20 Florida defeated Florida State 26-10 at Doak Campbell Stadium, securing its third consecutive victory over the Seminoles. However, the result carried much greater consequences for the home team. Florida State entered the Sunshine State rivalry needing one victory to qualify for a bowl game. Instead, the Seminoles will miss the postseason for the third consecutive season. Meanwhile, Florida celebrated a historic individual milestone and an impressive finish to its first regular season under coach Jon Sumrall. Florida Ends Florida State’s Bowl Hopes The Seminoles entered Friday with a 5-6 record and an opportunity to salvage their season. However, Florida’s defense made that task increasingly difficult. The Gators recorded six sacks, forced seven punts and intercepted Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels twice. Both interceptions came from defensive back J’Vari Flowers. Florida State struggled to sustain drives, converting just five of its 17 third-down opportunities. The Seminoles also went 1-for-4 on fourth down. Although Florida State finished with more total yards than Florida, the Gators consistently made the plays that mattered most. Consequently, the Seminoles finished their season at 5-7. The result marked Florida State’s third consecutive season without a bowl appearance, extending a frustrating stretch for one of college football’s most recognizable programs. Jadan Baugh Makes Florida History Against Seminoles Florida running back Jadan Baugh entered Friday needing just 20 rushing yards to accomplish a historic milestone. He finished with 77 yards on 19 carries and a touchdown. More importantly, Baugh became the first Florida running back to record consecutive 1,000-yard regular seasons under the program’s official statistical records. The achievement added another chapter to his impressive history against Florida State. Last season, Baugh rushed for 266 yards in Florida’s 40-21 victory over the Seminoles. That performance ranked among the greatest single-game rushing efforts in Florida history. Now, Baugh has another memorable accomplishment against his team’s biggest in-state rival. His 3-yard touchdown run in the first quarter gave Florida an early 7-0 lead. The Gators never trailed. item.title: Masked Ethan Brown shines in Illinois win
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Just four days ago, Illinois freshman guard Ethan Brown broke his nose in multiple different places. Two days ago, he got surgery to repair that broken nose, causing many to speculate that he may take some time off to rest and recover. That would not be the case. Friday night, Brown returned to the Illini starting lineup without skipping a beat, playing a key role in the team’s big win over the Western Kentucky Hilltoppers. First and foremost, it was a remarkable efficient night for the young guard from a scoring standpoint. He finished with 22 points while shooting 8-12 from the field, and 4-7 from downtown. He also stuffed the stat sheet, adding eight rebounds and four assists. Like usual, Brown played beyond his years in terms of making winning plays. In one sequence in the first half, he cleaned up a missed shot from Zavier Zens with an offensive rebound and putback on one possession, then dished out a clean pass to a cutting Zvonimir Ivisic for a transition dunk shortly after. Brown has been instrumental through the team’s first eight games, as he leads Illinois in both assists and rebounds, while also being a double-digit scorer on average.

item.title: Bronson Reed (Jermaine Haley) Shockingly Dies At 38
item.description: Bronson Reed died at 38 WWE WWE Superstar Bronson Reed shockingly died at 38 amid a serious kidney issues that led to undisclosed surgery earlier this month following his cameo at WWE Crown Jewel 12026 . After taking a bump off the stage through multiple tables, Reed remained in Saudi Arabia after suffering multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney following a garden-variety Beal toss from rising star Oba Femi. The spot appeared to go as planned, but Reed underwent surgery and recovery following the incident. Bronson Reed was a rising star in WWE, positioned prominently with top heel stable The Vision alongside the deliberate future of WWE in Logan Paul, Austin Theory, Bron Breakker and Paul Heyman, who has churned out countless mentees who became Hall of Famers under his guidance. Reed was known for his fast-paced style despite being a big man, and really excelled when he developed his flying splash finisher otherwise known as the Tsunami. Despite being a basic finisher in the context of 2026 pro wrestling, which is more high-risk than ever, Reed’s theatrical splash was a weekly highlight on WWE programming. The former New Japan Pro Wrestling standout was released by WWE in 2021, an incident which took him by surprise. The former NXT North American champion returned to WWE the following year and went on to reinvent himself as a more svelte big man, dropping over 100 pounds ahead of his 2026 return from injury. After suffering injuries at Crown Jewel, Reed’s surgery was believed to have been a success. “In great news, we are told Bronson Reed has made it back home and is continuing his recovery from surgery. Continued best wishes,” reported Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t WrestleZone .) Reed had previously suffered a fractured talus bone in November 2024 and a torn distal biceps in February 2026. Bronson is survived by his wife, high school sweetheart Paige Haley, and their two children, one of which is on the way. Reed was finally hitting his stride as a legitimate potential main eventer, and similar to fellow international star PAC—who passed away earlier this year—Bronson Reed is gone too soon. item.title: Back-end starter continues to build on underrated San Diego tenure
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Randy Vasquez #98 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Arizona Diamondbacks during the first inning at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Randy Vásquez Vásquez was an under-the-radar piece in the blockbuster trade between the Padres and the New York Yankees for superstar Juan Soto. Soto and Trent Grisham were sent to the Bronx, with Michael King being the headliner of the return. At the time, Vásquez had pitched quite well in the big leagues, with a 2.87 ERA in 37 2/3 innings. He blossomed into a back-end rotation piece in San Diego, breaking out in 2025 with a 3.84 ERA over 133 2/3 innings of work. Overall Grade: C+ He started off 2026 even better. Vásquez pitched to a 1.88 ERA through his first five starts and a 2.96 ERA through his first 10 outings. He regressed in June (7.84 ERA, 20.2 IP) before turning in a phenomenal August and September (2.76 ERA, 45.2 IP). Vásquez ended the season with career highs in innings pitched (140.2) and strikeouts (87) along with a career-low 1.27 WHIP. Overall, Vásquez had an incredible 2026 campaign. He built on his breakout in 2025 and pushed himself to become a better pitcher. His underlying metrics in 2025 suggested that most of his success was luck. 2026 proved that it wasn’t all coincidence. The underlying stats still aren’t kind to Vásquez (5.54 xERA, .288 xBA), but he’s managed to prove those stats wrong. There is always a question of whether that success will continue. However, with Vásquez as the only viable starter on the Padres’ current rotation, San Diego seems to trust the right-hander to fill out the back end of their rotation in 2027 and beyond.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
